what: THE ONE PLACE THE PROJECT'S EXPECTED CHECK AND FAILURE COUNTS LIVE. Written at Batch DE. `check_de.gd` reads this after every battery and reports; `docs/state.md` and `CLAUDE.md` POINT AT IT AND DO NOT RESTATE IT, because a second copy of a number is this project's oldest recurring defect.
how_a_row_moves: A BASELINE MOVES ONLY IN THE BATCH THAT CAUSES THE MOVEMENT, AND THE CHANGELOG SAYS WHY. Otherwise the table drifts into whatever the code happens to do.

fields.kind: suite | gate | scene | harness — chooses how the log is parsed.
fields.checks: [lo, hi] expected check count, or null when the target reports no readable count. THE FLOOR IS ASSERTED AND THE CEILING IS NOT: a FALLING count is an error, a RISING one is a notice.
fields.fails: [lo, hi] expected FAILURE count, or null when unreadable. THE POLARITY INVERTS: a RISING failure count is an error (the 48th failure among 47), a FALLING one is a notice.
fields.checks_obs / fails_obs: HOW MANY READINGS THE ROW RESTS ON. A band is a claim about a distribution nobody has characterised and the readings behind it are part of the claim — an's nine-observation band was exceeded on its tenth. THE COUNTING RULE: one per battery reading the record names from DC forward, plus DE's THREE (before on unmodified HEAD, after, and the final acceptance run) = 6, with named exceptions counted low where there is any doubt. A row whose FAILURE evidence differs from its CHECK evidence carries its own number — see test_batch_bo and test_rune_battle.
fields.expect: optional: a verdict substring that must appear, for a target that reports no counts at all.
fields.flake: optional: a KNOWN flake and its observed rate. Its failure count is carried as a band for that reason.
fields.note: optional: why this row is what it is.

check_cl_width.note: REPORTS NEITHER COUNT NOR FAILURES — the battery cannot see whether it passed at all. Recorded so the state is a ratchet rather than a blind spot.

check_cm_live.note: THE ONE RED THAT IS ON PURPOSE. Identical on unmodified HEAD, recorded as owed in the gate itself. It is the only thing pressing the defensive bar.

check_map.note: ITS `fails` FIGURE IS ITS OWN `reach-contiguity failures: N` LINE, not a suite tally — that is what the battery's grep reads here too, and it is a real number worth ratcheting. Not a hang: ~99% CPU for about five minutes. The battery gives it a 600s bound.

check_map_screen.note: REPORTS NEITHER COUNT NOR FAILURES. Its whole verdict is the one line in `expect`, which is why that line is pinned.

check_parse.note: Walks res://scripts and res://scenes only — it does NOT cover the suites, the gates or the two fixtures. Its verdict is read off stderr, never off a tally: a --script target whose base class does not resolve prints a parse error, runs not one line, and EXITS 0.

flake.rate: 2 red in 15 readings — roughly 1 in 7, and BOTH reds landed under machine load
flake.what: § pyromancer: `rune_resist_pierce never fired against a resistant warband` — the White Flame's only read site, asserted by driving a LIVE battle against a fire-resistant warband and looking for `Rune: the flame bites through resistance` in a snapshot or the log. The proc has to actually land; test_rune_battle calls seed() ZERO times.

test_rune_battle.note: FOUND BY `check_de` ON ITS FIRST ACCEPTANCE RUN AND PREVIOUSLY UNRECORDED. Its CHECK count is rock steady at 97 across all 15 readings — only the failure moves, which is the flake signature CLAUDE.md names. READINGS: clean in DE's before- and after-batteries, RED in the final acceptance battery, RED on the next ad-hoc run, then TEN CONSECUTIVE CLEAN runs on an idle machine. BOTH REDS LANDED UNDER LOAD, which is a hypothesis and not a finding — the assertion's own comment says the snapshot 'is the one that cannot race', so a race is the thing to look at first. THE FIX IS THE `at`/`bo` SHAPE (seed the draw, or assert on the snapshot alone) AND IT IS DELIBERATELY LEFT FOR ITS OWN BATCH: one flake at a time is how the effect stays attributable. SEEDED AT DF §0, per-site: `_seeded()` immediately before the forced hit and nowhere else, so the other 96 checks keep their own stream. THE BAND IS DELIBERATELY NOT TIGHTENED — two clean post-seed readings cannot retire a rate measured over fifteen, and tightening on that evidence is the same fault as writing a band from too few readings, in the opposite direction. The failure message now carries the state the forced hit happened in (battle_over, both units' liveness, the target's fire resist, the pierce fraction), so the NEXT red says what was missing instead of only that it was missing.
